ORDERING: this record's first commit contains the five rows below together with the whole A2 baseline and the A3 authority derivation; `git status --porcelain` at that commit shows ONLY .agents/v2/evidence/ paths, and internal/application/loop.go, internal/application/loop_test.go, internal/application/completion_proof_guard_test.go, internal/runner/controlplane.go, internal/runner/loopdriver.go and cmd/runner/main_test.go do not yet exist. ROW 1 -- WHAT THIS TASK MAKES TRUE. One bounded pass, Service.LoopPass, in one new file internal/application/loop.go, gated callerActor(ctx, RoleScheduler) and that role ALONE, called from the EXISTING InternalReconcile closure at cmd/control-plane/main.go:199-207 inside the EXISTING 5s timeout at :200, on the context that ALREADY carries the scheduler identity internal/api/api.go:114 mints with application.LoopCaller and :119 attaches. Four stages, each carrying the observation that justified it: stage W issues domain.RequirementWait for a `ready` Requirement whose scheduler.Decision is unassigned with Reason in exactly {resource-conflict, no-runner-capacity}; stage R issues domain.RequirementRecover for an `active` or `waiting` Requirement one of whose Increments has an Execution in domain.ExecutionLost; stage D calls the EXISTING Service.Plan and Service.Prepare for a `ready` Requirement the scheduler ASSIGNED, which is the severed edge that makes POST /v1/runner/claims:acquire and /v1/executions/* reachable at all; stage P calls release.Pipeline.Promote and carries the domain.StableReleaseProof it returns through domain.RequirementEvaluate into domain.CompleteRequirementFromRelease, in ONE transaction, only for a Requirement all of whose Increments reached domain.IncrementReleased. One new runner-role read, Service.OfferedWork, behind one new route GET /v1/runner/work declared in contracts/openapi/openapi-v1.yaml. One new standard-library control-plane client internal/runner/controlplane.go and one bounded driver internal/runner/loopdriver.go. cmd/runner gains a real mode. One application-level release-source constructor so cmd/control-plane can attach the observer WITHOUT importing internal/release. ROW 2 -- WHAT IT DELIBERATELY DOES NOT DO. It adds NO second producer of a scheduler identity (internal/application/caller.go and internal/application/requested_by_test.go are prohibited; application.LoopCaller stays the only one and V2-086's scan is re-run unedited). It gives NO path an identity it is not: the driver never constructs an application.Caller and internal/runner/orchestrator.go -- whose line 54 fabricates application.Caller{Role: RoleRunner, ...} with no session verification -- is PROHIBITED and byte-unchanged. It issues NO domain.RequirementPause, NO domain.RequirementCancel, NO domain.RequirementResume (owner verbs, landed by V2-090), NO domain.RequirementNeedInput (internal/application/human_input.go is prohibited), NO domain.RequirementStart (V2-084 landed it inside Service.Claim), and NO post-execution Increment command (verify, integrate, preview-validate, accept, release). It adds NO RequirementCommandKind, NO RequirementStatus, NO PermitKind, NO port, NO allowed() list entry, NO read-model change, NO environment-variable-derived default release root, NO ci component edge, NO Makefile change, NO store change and NO index. It runs NO Provider CLI and posts NO Execution result: all three provider adapters return provider.NoExec, so a driver that accepted a result would be accepting one it did not obtain. ROW 3 -- WHAT IT RECORDS BUT DOES NOT FIX. (a) domain.RequirementWait from `active` and from `recovering` stays UNISSUED: application.AllocationSchedulerStatus maps `active` to scheduler.StatusAssigned and every status other than ready/active/completed to the empty status, and scheduler.structurallyReady requires StatusReady, so the scheduler can never attach a capacity or contention reason to an active or recovering Requirement. (b) Three of scheduler.AllReasons' seven members are UNREACHABLE from application.BuildAllocationSnapshot -- unmet-dependency (the rows carry no Dependencies), repository-unavailable (Snapshot.Repositories is one synthetic entry with no FailureCount and no IsolatedUntil) and not-executable (Assessment is never set). (c) A Requirement whose Execution is domain.ExecutionFailed rather than domain.ExecutionLost gets NO transition, while docs/architecture/domain-model.md:275 says such a Requirement should become recovering, waiting or needs-input. (d) internal/reconciler/reconciler.go's recoverOne acts as domain.NewActorID("reconciler"), a name the component makes up for itself, and internal/reconciler holds no application.Caller at all; the Requirement transition therefore cannot live there and the reconciler's output is read as an OBSERVATION instead. (e) application.allocationReport at internal/application/allocation.go:603 DISCARDS the page's `more` flag, so the owner queue read cannot say whether it saw everything; internal/application/allocation.go is prohibited, so the pass makes its OWN u.RequirementsPage call and keeps both return values rather than repairing that line. (f) application.Event has eight fields and no payload, and internal/application/ports.go and internal/store/** are prohibited, so a transition's justifying observation is carried on the DURABLE RECORD the same s.record call writes (the idempotency ResponseJSON, in the same transaction) plus the event's own Type, not on a new Event field. (g) The api-contract chain position and the M3live re-observation fact recorded under A25/A26. ROW 4 -- WHAT ONLY A LATER TASK CAN ESTABLISH. The IAP authentication boundary, idle scale-to-zero, real Firestore permissions and contention, and the deploy path: docs/architecture/release-contract.md:49 places all four with the initial deploy gate D1 and preview-local cannot establish them. A promotion over a FULLY EVIDENCED candidate, because the shipped configuration cannot assemble one and this task fabricates none -- so the completion transition's claim stops at COMPONENT grade. Any real-Provider observation, because no Provider CLI invocation is authorised here. ROW 5 -- DOES IT PASS ANY RELEASE GATE. NO. This task passes no gate and issues no gate verdict.

checks.name: product-authority
checks.summary: A3 PRODUCT AUTHORITY, derived and quoted with the file and line MEASURED (every line number in A3 agreed exactly with the Work Order; there is no disagreement in this item). docs/architecture/domain-model.md:265 ready = '優先順位評価済みで実行可能'; :266 active = '1つ以上のIncrementが進行中'; :267 waiting = 'dependency、capacity、time条件を自動待機'; :270 recovering = 'lost ExecutionやPreview failureから再開中'; :271 evaluating = 'Stableで課題が解決したか評価中'; :272 completed = '対応Stable ReleaseとEvidenceで課題解決を確認'; :275 '`failed`をRequirementの終端状態にしない。failureはExecution、Provider Run、Evidenceに記録し、Requirementはrecovering、waiting、needs-inputのいずれかになる。'; :101 '1 Requirementに複数Incrementを許す。Incrementが成功してもRequirementは自動完了しない。'; docs/product/user-facing-spec.md:272 waiting = '外部資源、依存、時間条件などを待ち、自動的に再評価される'; :275 recovering = 'failureまたはRunner消失後、安全な再開を行っている'; docs/product/definition.md:105 'Previewで実証され、Stableへ昇格した時点とする'; :111 '3. 利用可能なworkerが、実行可能なRequirementを排他的にclaimする。'; :130 '完了を自己申告だけで決めず、要求と不変条件を検証する'. THE FOUR CONCLUSIONS, stated plainly: (1) waiting is justified by a capacity or contention or dependency condition and by nothing else, so it is NOT a general 'nothing happened' bucket; (2) recovering is justified by a lost Execution or a lost Runner, which is exactly what internal/reconciler already writes when it expires a Lease past its TTL and calls domain.MarkExecutionLost; (3) completion is bound to a Stable promotion and is NEVER granted by an Increment succeeding; (4) an Increment existing at all is the precondition for the whole claim surface, which is why the severed Increment-creation path is the same defect as the two unreachable Requirement transitions. This reading does not differ from the design packet's, so no escalation is raised on A3.
